proposals.hypothesis: The closest result so far is the trihalo-BQ with one open C-H (2,3-dichloro-5-fluoro: f 1.17, margin 0.157). It kept the margin above 0.15 and lost less binding than the tetrahalo BQs (D14 f 0.72, D11 f 0.28). D07 (bind -25.8, f 1.24) and D08 (bind -24.3, no detachment) both support small halogens with an open C-H. I promote that direction and flip the halogen ratio to two F and one Cl on D08's frame. F is smaller than Cl, so it should cost less carbonyl-region crowding and keep the CO2 binding. The one Cl and two F should still lift the margin toward 0.15 or more, since D08 (F4) reached 0.178. This tests whether the F-rich trihalo pattern gets more binding than the Cl-rich one. I avoid CN (D03, D06, D10 detached CO2) and NH2/OH (D01, D02, D04, D05 lowered f), and I avoid Br and a full set of heavy halogens (D11). K084 and K020 report CO2 adducts for F4-BQ and a dichloro-BQ. Risk: f is unlikely to reach 2, since no reference has, so the best realistic outcome is f above 1.2 with a margin of at least 0.15.
